masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A wooden carved face mask with feather nose ornament and wicker backing, consistent with Sepik-region ritual masks and specifically attributed to the Mundugumor by the 1936 museum register.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: Carved wood ceremonial face mask with shell eyes, pigment decoration and fibre attachments, directly attributed by the museum to Mundugumor makers — a classic Sepik-region ritual mask type.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden ancestral figure with shell-inlaid eyes and elongated form, consistent with Mundugumor (Biwat/Sepik region) ancestor figures used in ritual contexts; the museum attributes it directly to this group.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden ancestral figure with shell-inlaid eyes, standing on a tiered conical base — a classic Sepik-region ancestor figure form consistent with Mundugumor carving traditions, and the museum explicitly credits the Mundugumor as makers.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A wooden ancestral figure with shell-inlaid eyes, carved in a squatting pose typical of Sepik/Mundugumor woodcarving, matching the museum's attribution to Mundugumor makers.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden ancestral figure with a stylized hook-like torso, large eyes, and pierced ears, consistent with Mundugumor (Biwat/Yuat River region) ancestor figures used in ritual contexts; museum attributes manufacture directly to this group.

instruments.name: drum
instruments.title: drum
instruments.reason: A carved wooden slit/hand drum with incised decoration and two carved head finials with fiber attachments, a classic Sepik-region instrument type, consistent with Mundugumor material culture and directly attributed to them by the museum.

instruments.name: slit-drum
instruments.title: slit-drum
instruments.reason: A carved wooden slit drum with animal-form handles at each end, decorated with incised spiral and curvilinear motifs and inset cowrie shells — a classic Sepik-region ceremonial instrument, consistent with Mundugumor manufacture and use.
